MX17 at LNL · target options · 22 Oct 2026 · status 11 Nov 2026

Metallic lithium is the right film and at LNL the heat is easy: both still hold. The 22 Oct recommendation, lithium on molybdenum on a thin diamond, is superseded. The Mo and the diamond were dropped on 11 Nov, and the film should be 10–12 µm until its chemistry in the beam-line vacuum is measured.

A thermal model of every backing, nuclear yields from measured data for what the film and backing emit, and Geant4 (run L9) of the leptons through the target assembly. Slide 2 gives the status after the buildability review of 11 Nov and the design now proposed.

Details

Pierfrancesco's reply to the LNL slides: the target is the critical issue. No fluorine; heat; the backing's background and the best backing; a cold trap for carbon; PIGE monitoring; the 441 keV γ and the window; the strip/clamp design; and his proposal of 20 µm Li on 1 mm diamond with micro-channel cooling. Each slide answers one of these. Write-up: lnl/target/TARGET_OPTIONS.md; the earlier fluorine/heat study is the note lnl-lithium-target.

Updated 11 Nov 2026 with the buildability review (lnl/target/TARGET_REVIEW.md). The study's first recommendation (20 µm Li / Mo 8 µm / CVD diamond 50–100 µm, later the 45° diamond window) is kept as a record and marked as superseded. The cap's days: estimate: the 45° diamond window’s Geant4 days (same geometry; ray-trace: aluminium for diamond changes σ68 by 0.0–0.5°); Geant4 run L14 pending. The review is a proposal. It has not yet been discussed with Pierfrancesco.

Where this stands (11 Nov 2026): the lithium film and the physics hold, the Mo layer and the diamond are dropped

The buildability review checked every design against how lithium targets are really made. The review is a proposal. It has not yet been discussed with Pierfrancesco.

Details

Source: lnl/target/TARGET_REVIEW.md (11 Nov 2026), read into the decks through lnl/target/review_data.py. Days: the reference fit of nd_reach.csv (θ × |y| × E_sum, background shape floating). For the cap: estimate: the 45° diamond window’s Geant4 days (same geometry; ray-trace: aluminium for diamond changes σ68 by 0.0–0.5°); Geant4 run L14 pending.

How lithium targets are really made: No laboratory was found that deposits Li, Cu or Ti inside the beam pipe. Li metal is always made off the line (glovebox, or an evaporation stand with a vacuum transfer). A 20 µm film does not need more: a few nm to ~0.5 µm of surface compound from the transfer is ≤ 3 % of it.

The flat assembly this deck recommended (Li 20 µm / Mo 8 µm / diamond 50 µm on a Cu ring in a CFRP chamber) carries both dropped parts, and most of its parts are new to LNL. With the reference fit it reached 0.23 d per µA with the big plastics. The AN2000 group ran 24 thin LiF films on self-supporting backings: most gave 6–8 h of stable rate, the best two days; their one Li₂O film broke at once. Hanoi’s films were "punctured many times".

The cap's numbers: at 1 bar the 0.4 mm face is at 80 MPa (×3.5 on yield), 0.5 mm at 51 MPa (×5.4) (estimate, clamped ellipse 20 × 28 mm). Cost < 1 k€ a piece, 1–3 weeks (estimate).

Superseded on 11 Nov: the 22 Oct recommendation, Li on Mo on a thin diamond. The Mo and the diamond are dropped

A record. The lithium, the cold trap and the monitoring carry over to the aluminium end cap (slide 2). Hover the layers.

3

Details

Mo (or Ta) between the Li and the diamond did three jobs: it stopped the 0.87 MeV protons (range 6 µm), so the hydrogen landed in a metal that tolerates ≥ 3.4×10¹⁹ /cm²; it carried the beam current away (diamond is an insulator); and it gave lithium something to wet, which an untreated diamond surface may not. The diamond's only job was to carry the heat.

11 Nov 2026 (TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.3, §4.5). Mo: The Geant4 x-ray check of 4 Nov doubled the Mo K yield: 19–45 % Micromegas occupancy per arm per µA, and no thin wall absorbs 17.5 keV. These designs would have to run at 0.2–0.5 µA. Diamond: At 1 µA the beam is 1.1 W; a 0.4 mm aluminium face carries it with a 5 K rise. The diamond is brittle, has never been hydrogen-tested, costs 6–15 k€ mounted (estimate), and carries the Mo stop. The 45° geometry is kept, in aluminium. In the cap the copper does the Mo's three jobs and the aluminium wall carries the heat and the vacuum.

Metallic lithium gives ×8.2 the ⁸Be rate per proton at 20 µm (still holds). Use 10–12 µm until the hydroxide rate is measured

11 Nov: the film recommendation changes from “15–25 µm” to 10–12 µm until the conversion rate is measured (green; slide “Li → LiOH”). That keeps 51–61 % of the 20 µm yield, still ×4.2–5.1 the thin Li₂O film. A fresh film of any thickness up to 20 µm stays clear of the 441 keV resonance. A converted one does not.

Details

opt_backing.py + target_model.layered_yield → stacks.csv. The X17 is normalised per total γ₀ as in FEAS (ATOMKI 2022 reported the anomaly in direct capture too). If it came from the M1 resonance only, the 20 µm gain is ×6.7. The 3D fit absorbs a known energy profile; a 20 % 441 share biases it by < 0.06 R_ATOMKI (TARGET_STUDY §8), so 0.85 % is negligible.

11 Nov 2026: the 12 and 15 µm bars and the film recommendation come from the buildability review (review_li_conversion.py → review_li_conversion.csv, same yield model). The 441 shares on this slide are for a fresh metal film. Half of a 20 µm Li film turned to LiOH by residual water takes a 1.10 MeV beam down to 454 keV: 52 % of the γ₀ then comes from the 441 keV resonance (fresh 0.85 %; 91 % at 1.03 MeV). 10–12 µm of Li stays at or below 10 % even fully converted, for 51–61 % of the yield. LNL's CN group rolls foils of 10–40 µm, “down to sub-10 µm” (arXiv:2605.12005).

Details

11 Nov 2026 (TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.5, §6.1): the aluminium face is not in the 22 Oct model. Its rise is the closed form ΔT = P/(2πkt)·[ln(a/r_spot) + ½] for a 0.4 mm 6061 disc (4.6 K at 1.1 W, 18.6 K at 4.4 W; a 0.5 mm face 3.7 K), plus about 6 K along the end piece. The film stays near room temperature. LNL's Cu cup is air-cooled at about 10 °C per watt and safe to ~10 W (arXiv:2605.12005). The diamond curves stay as a record: micro-channels (352 µA) and a brazed 1 mm diamond (485 µA) are for machines of tens of µA.

opt_thermal.py. Checks: a conduction-only disk agrees with the analytic Gaussian-source result to 0.7 %; the 10 µm Al disk of the earlier study gives 97.6 °C against 95 °C. Contacts: dry clamp 5×10³–10⁴ W/m²/K, braze 2×10⁵, water 2×10⁴, micro-channels as h_eff = 3×10⁴ (laminar, 200 × 300 µm channels at 400 µm pitch, 1 L/min, Δp 1.2 bar). Limits: Li film 150 °C, Li₂O 300 °C. LNL beam power is 1.1 W/µA: the issue on a thin foil is the conduction path, not the power.

Why the slide-7 clamp failed: 20 µm of Li conducts k·t = 1.7 mW/K sideways, 1 mm of diamond 1.8 W/K. The backing must be the conductor.

For high-current machines only, not LNL (diamond dropped 11 Nov): above ~30 µA the contacts set the temperature, not the diamond

A record of the diamond study. 1 mm diamond, 20 µm Li, 100 µA: vary the rim-clamp contact and the Li/diamond interface

rim clamp to the cooled ring

Li/diamond interface

A dry clamp in vacuum (10³–10⁴) is the bottleneck: braze or indium. CVD-diamond gyrotron windows are brazed to Cu cuffs and edge-cooled the same way.

Nobody seems to have measured evaporated Li on diamond. A Ta/Mo/Ti layer (carbide-forming) is the standard fix, and the same layer stops the beam: one bench test answers it.

Diamond grade: k = 1000 instead of 1800 adds ~20 K at 100 µA. Irrelevant at LNL.

Inputs: ⁷Li(p,p′γ) from Bykov et al. ARI 175 (2021) (thick Li 4.9×10⁶ /µC at 1.0 MeV); ¹³C(p,γ) 556 keV resonance from Skowronski et al. Resonances are integrated analytically per energy step (checked against (λ²/2)ωγ/ε). Ta/Cu Coulomb excitation (≤ 1.1 MeV) not computed. No neutrons below E_p = 1.88 MeV.

8

Details

X₀ only matters for a backing in the leptons’ path, i.e. a target at the centre; at +12 cm (Geant4 L9) the backing is behind the leptons.

11 Nov 2026 (TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.3, §4.5–4.7, §6.5). Mo: The Geant4 x-ray check of 4 Nov doubled the Mo K yield: 19–45 % Micromegas occupancy per arm per µA, and no thin wall absorbs 17.5 keV. These designs would have to run at 0.2–0.5 µA. Diamond: At 1 µA the beam is 1.1 W; a 0.4 mm aluminium face carries it with a 5 K rise. The diamond is brittle, has never been hydrogen-tested, costs 6–15 k€ mounted (estimate), and carries the Mo stop. The 45° geometry is kept, in aluminium. Be: The last supplier of machined and welded beryllium vacuum tubes stopped in 2023 (CERN now makes its own). A custom thin shell is 20–60 k€ and 6–12 months (estimate), plus a safety case, and all the Be designs carry the Mo stop. Copper: LNL's CN group presses its rolled Li on a 300 µm Cu cup that also stops the beam. Hydrogen in copper is a watch item, not a blocker: the blister thresholds were measured at 2 MeV and BNCT current densities, and MEG II stopped 8–11 µA in 25 µm of Cu for four weeks with no significant deterioration. Tantalum is the standard backing at this energy (LUNA, PTB) because it takes up hydrogen without blistering: a 10 µm Ta stop costs +0.4° in the ray-trace and its L x-rays stop in the same aluminium. Aluminium in the beam is still to be avoided (it alloys with Li and has the 992 keV resonance): in the cap the Cu covers the whole face and the first centimetre of the bore.

Lithium is a getter: the cold trap must pump the water as well as the carbon (still holds). Corrected 11 Nov: what the hydroxide does to a thick film

An upper limit: every molecule sticks. LiOH passivates the surface, so the real rate is lower. Nobody has published it for a thick film under beam.

Corrected 11 Nov. “The products stay on the target, so the Li is not lost” is true for the thin Li₂O film only. In a 20 µm metal film the lithium atoms stay, but the added oxygen and hydrogen slow the beam down to the 441 keV resonance (next slide).

Carbon, 14 days at 1 µA with no trap: γ₀ ×0.85 on the 20 µm Li, 441 share 2.3%; with a cold shield ×1.00. Carbon is a 441 keV-calibration problem, not a 1 MeV one.

9

Details

Hydrogen: Budker INP in-situ blistering under 2 MeV protons (Cu from 10¹⁹ /cm², dense at 3×10¹⁹; Ta unchanged at 3.4×10¹⁹, ≥ 6.7×10²⁰ claimed); diamond: 1.2×10¹⁷ /cm² at 350 keV blistered only after a > 1400 °C anneal, no MeV/room-temperature data found. Water/O₂: Hertz–Knudsen flux × sticking ≈ 1 on fresh Li (ESTIMATE ×3); the products stay on the target and dilute it. 11 Nov 2026 (TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.2): the 22 Oct conclusion “the yield per µC drops slowly” was checked for the thin Li₂O film only. For a 20 µm metal film the main effect is the added stopping power, shown on the next slide. A vacuum transfer leaves ~6 nm of Li₂O (BINP) and even ~0.5 µm of hydroxide from a short argon-bag or air transfer is 2–3 % of a 20 µm film: what converts the film is the days it spends in the beam-line vacuum. Carbon: ~1 C retained per proton without a trap (Peterson & Laubert 1977), ×10 less with a cold shield, none seen with a LN₂ trap at 10⁻⁷ mbar (Redigolo 2024). opt_backing.py, opt_monitor.py.

New (11 Nov): a 20 µm Li film half turned to LiOH gives 52 % of its γ₀ at the 441 keV resonance. 12 µm: 10 % at most

Residual water turns lithium into LiOH. The lithium atoms stay, but the oxygen and hydrogen add stopping, so the beam slows further. E_p = 1.10 MeV

20 µm, half converted: the beam leaves the film at 454 keV instead of 872. The 441 keV resonance is ~50× stronger than the 18.15 MeV one, so the 17.64 MeV line takes over and the trigger rate rises several-fold.

Film: 10–12 µm until the conversion rate is measured, not 15–25 µm. Fully converted, 12 µm gives at most 10 % and 10 µm 2.7 %, for 61 % and 51 % of the 20 µm yield.

10

Details

lnl/target/review_li_conversion.py (the repo's yield model, PSTAR stopping; the outer fraction of the Li atoms converted, the rest metal) → lnl/out/target/options/review_li_conversion.csv. TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.2.

Half of a 20 µm Li film turned to LiOH by residual water takes a 1.10 MeV beam down to 454 keV: 52 % of the γ₀ then comes from the 441 keV resonance (fresh 0.85 %; 91 % at 1.03 MeV). 10–12 µm of Li stays at or below 10 % even fully converted, for 51–61 % of the yield. The rate is unknown: 1.35 µm a day at 10⁻⁷ mbar of water if every molecule sticks (an upper limit; LiOH passivates). A one-week film test on the LNL line decides the thickness.

It applies to every design, the Cu cup and the Cu ogive included: it is a property of the film, not of the shell. It did not matter for LNL's neutron work, where the film's energy loss only shapes the neutron spectrum. The fit-bias test of the lithium-target note covered a drift of the 441 share up to 20 %, not this. With the repo's upper-limit rate half of a 20 µm film is hydroxide after 7.4 days at 10⁻⁷ mbar of water and after 0.74 days at 10⁻⁶ mbar. The real rate is lower: LiOH passivates the surface, and BINP and PTB both report a compound layer that grows slowly during operation.

What the thinner film costs in days to 3σ at the ATOMKI strength, 1 µA, big plastics (the 45° window, Geant4 L10, as a stand-in for the cap; a yield and line-mix change only): 20 µm: 0.31 d (4.2 as built) · 12 µm: 0.43 d (5.5 as built) · 10 µm: 0.51 d (6.3 as built). With the big plastics the fit is limited by the background shape, so the cost is less than proportional.

What to do: (1) a 10–12 µm film; (2) run at 1.10 MeV; (3) watch the γ₀ yield per µC, which rises several times when the beam reaches 441 keV (a LaBr₃ or the Ge planned for PIGE separates 17.64 from 18.15 MeV), and replace the target when the share passes a few per cent; (4) measure the rate before the run: one film on the AN2000 or CN line for a week at the vacuum we will have, following 478 keV and γ₀; (5) keep the cold trap upstream, and no PVC next to the target if it can be avoided.

If Li₂O forms instead of LiOH the effect is much smaller: a fully oxidised 20 µm film gives 5.6 % at 1.10 MeV.

Details

11 Nov 2026: every 20 µm Li stack in this run carries Mo, Ta or diamond, all dropped by the buildability review, and the flat target in a CFRP chamber is not pursued. The rule the run gave carries over: in the aluminium end cap the leptons cross a 0.4–0.5 mm face at 45° and a 0.5 mm end piece. Its days: 0.31 d with the big plastics, 4.2 / 6.5 d as built (liquid repaired / as at n_TOF) (estimate: the 45° diamond window’s Geant4 days (same geometry; ray-trace: aluminium for diamond changes σ68 by 0.0–0.5°); Geant4 run L14 pending).

Geant4 L9 (MX17_Full_Geant branch lnl_target, multi-layer backings): per configuration 5×10⁵ X17 (m 16.8), 5×10⁵ M1 and 5×10⁵ E1 Born IPC at 18.15 MeV, 2×10⁷ ⁸Be γ (EPC). Big plastics, LNL-calibrated calorimetry, MM 15° + TOF, the opening angle and pointing about the target position. Reach: Asimov/Fisher fit in θ × |y| × n_down with M1, E1, γ₁ and EPC norms free, cosmics fixed, best E_sum window; scaled so the baseline equals the reference 3D fit (FEAS §14, 1.0 d at 1 µA). γ₁ uses the baseline L2 templates for every configuration. Per µA: the 20 µm Li films make ×8.2 the γ₀, so their days per µA include that gain; "µA for the baseline rate" is the current that gives the baseline's X17 rate.

Details

Full-energy efficiency at 478 keV, 10 cm: 60 % HPGe 4×10⁻³, 3″×3″ LaBr₃ 6×10⁻³ (±30 %), scaled as 1/d². Total rate ~4× the peak (ESTIMATE). Sensitivity: 10 % less Li → −7 to −9 % in the 478 yield; 10 µg/cm² carbon → −0.6 %. Window: XCOM μ/ρ(Al) 0.0838 (0.478 MeV), 0.0227 cm²/g (17.6 MeV); pair conversion (7/9) t/X₀; Highland at 8.6 MeV. opt_monitor.py.

11 Nov 2026: the monitoring carries over unchanged to the aluminium end cap, and it gains a second job. The 478 keV line follows the lithium content, which does not change when the film turns to hydroxide. The alarm for the hydroxide is the γ₀ yield per µC and the 17.64 MeV line: both rise several-fold when the beam reaches 441 keV inside the film (TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.2).

Details

lxplus/g4tendl_check.py → g4tendl_check.csv.

what to test and what to ask, revised 11 Nov 2026

Tests that decide the design now

1. One Li film on the AN2000 or CN line for a week, at the vacuum we will have, following the 478 keV and γ₀ lines: the conversion rate, and so the film thickness.

2. 10–15 µm of Cu on a flat aluminium face, coated below ~150 °C: adhesion, a thermal-cycled coupon.

3. A pressure test of every cap. A fast valve upstream.

4. Geant4 run L14, the aluminium cap: running.

No longer asked for (diamond and Mo dropped): protons on diamond, Li on coated diamond, a brazed diamond membrane.

Questions for Pierfrancesco

1. How will the Li go on his ogive: pressed foil, or the evaporator of his 2015 paper?

2. Would he consider a flat face at 45°? It keeps his rolled and pressed Li and removes the flank.

3. Can the workshop turn a 0.4–0.5 mm Al wall, and who puts 10–15 µm of Cu on it, cool?

4. The vacuum at the target: pressure, residual gas, PVC or ceramic insulator.

5. How thin can a rolled foil be made reproducibly (we would like 8–12 µm), and how does it travel?

The review is a proposal. It has not yet been discussed with Pierfrancesco. Current options: lnl-target-compare.

14

Details

Revised 11 Nov 2026 from TARGET_REVIEW.md §4.2, §7 and §8. The 22 Oct list asked for five tests, three of them on diamond (MeV protons on bare and coated CVD diamond, Li on Mo/Ta-coated diamond, a brazed 50–100 µm membrane), and asked whether LNL could coat and mount a diamond membrane. The open point that remains from that list is the Li target at a known water pressure followed by PIGE: it is now the test that decides the film thickness. The full list of questions is in TARGET_REVIEW.md §7 (we do not need anything deposited in the beam pipe; the beam spot, as before).
